menu.reconcile_note: The two on-target items resolve the indirect calls that decide the verdict. The item for *0x447f64 shows it is sym.imp.read_csman: it fills auStack_30 with the STORED security answer read from config-store id 0x80010400 (a server-provisioned value, not request input) and reads the enable flag from id 0x201500. The item for *0x4480c0 shows it is sym.imp.strcasecmp: the grant (return 0) is reached only when the submitted user_ans equals that stored answer, and every mismatch or missing-param path returns 0xffffffff (deny). The caller sym.do_login treats return 0 as success. So in the ORIGINAL body the only way to be authorized is to submit the answer that matches the provisioned stored answer; there is no literal secret and no request-controllable expected value on the path, so the gate is sound: not-vulnerable. Both items are independently necessary: without the read_csman item the buffer auStack_30 is filled by an unresolved indirect call and could hold a literal or attacker value, and without the strcasecmp item the compare that guards the grant is unresolved; dropping either leaves the verdict undecidable. This same menu does not neutralize the mutant flaw, because the flaw lives inside the mutant body, not in these callees. zyxel-0x402ae8-M1 (hardcoded-backdoor-cred) injects an extra branch right after the user_ans param is found: if (**0x447f6c)(submitted value, "__zyxsvc__") == 0 then return 0, before the genuine strcasecmp. The literal "__zyxsvc__" and the grant both sit in the mutant body. Knowing that *0x447f64 is read_csman and *0x4480c0 is strcasecmp does not touch that injected literal branch, so any attacker who submits user_ans=__zyxsvc__ is authorized regardless of the stored answer, and the mutant still resolves to vulnerable under the same context.
